title: Remove One Element to Split Equally

reported.text: Remove exactly one element from an array, then decide whether the remaining array can be split into two subarrays with equal sum.

sources.passage:
Google India L3 || Interview Experience || Offer Accepted
Hey Everyone, Im sharing my recent Google Software Engineer L3 interview experience. 
The LeetCode Discuss section helped me a lot in my prep and its time for me to give back to the community.

There were total 4 Interviews.
1. Virtual Technical round
2. Virtual googliness round
3. Onsite Technical round
4. Onsite Technical round


---


**Virtual Technical Round**
Question: A variation of [https://leetcode.com/problems/maximum-good-subarray-sum](https://leetcode.com/problems/maximum-good-subarray-sum) in which we have to return any pair of indices {i, j} rather than the max sum.

---


**Virtual Googliness Round**
Simple behavioural and hypothetical questions.

---
**Onsite Technical Rounds**
Both the rounds were on the same day, back to back in Google's office.
Two different interviewers and two different questions.

Question1: 
It was a story wrapped question but the crux of the questions was,
Given a string consisting of only 2 letters 'a' and 'b' such that the number of 'a' and number of 'b' is even in the string. You can make at most 2 cuts in the string and divide the sub-strings amongst Alice and Bob in such a way that the number of 'a' Alice has == number of 'a' bob has and number of 'b' Alice has == number of 'b' bob has. Return the index or indices of the cut(s).

Question2:
Another story wrapped question but the crux was,
Given an array of integers in one operation you will select any element from the array and remove it from the array then you have to tell that is it possible to divide that new array into two subarrays such that the sum of the subarrays is equal (after doing the operation).




---

I was able to solve every question and was give a positive verdict in each round. (Was told to work on my time management as a feedback)
After completing all the rounds my recruiter called me in 2 days to tell me that I have cleared the interviews and my profile is being sent for team-matching stage, got a team match in 2 business days, had a good talk with the manager. Then came the Hiring Committee, in which my packet was sent to the HC, after 3 days recruiter called for Compensation discussion and on the same day got the offer.


---

If anybody needs some tips on how I did it, I would just say, to believe in yourself because any day your destiny can change and you would want to be ready to

Google ML Engineer (L4/L5) Interview Experience, Hire?
# 🚀 Google ML Engineer (L4/L5) Interview Experience, Hire? 🤞

**Total Rounds:** 4 (2 Virtual + 2 Onsite)

I recently went through the Google ML loop and wanted to share a realistic breakdown — including mistakes, recoveries, and where things could go either way.

---

## 🔹 Round 1 — ML System Design (Virtual)

**Problem:** Design a Google Reviews–like system

We covered:
- NLP pipeline for reviews
- Deep dive into BERT
- Trade-offs: LLMs vs smaller models (latency, cost, quality)
- Unsupervised techniques for clustering / summarization

💡 Strong back-and-forth, deep discussion on modeling choices

**Verdict:** Hire (H) / Strong Hire (SH)

---

## 🔹 Round 2 — Googliness (Virtual)

Behavioral + situational:
- Ambiguous scenarios
- “Most complex project”
- Decision-making under uncertainty

⚠️ What went wrong:
- Answers weren’t as structured
- Missed depth in a few responses

📩 Recruiter feedback: Mixed

**Verdict:** Leaning Hire (LH)

---

## 🔹 Round 3 — Onsite Coding (Graphs + Heaps)

### Problem:
- Movies with similarity relationships (transitive)
- Query:
  - Highest-rated movie
  - Tie → lexicographically smallest
  - Follow-up → Top K movies

### Approach:
1. Build graph
2. DFS to get connected component
3. Initially used max heap

💥 Twist:
Interviewer questioned heap usage → suggested a variable

👉 Then came follow-up: Top K movies

### Recovery:
- Switched to min heap of size K
- Remove smallest when size exceeds K

💡 Initial approach scaled well for follow-up

⚠️ Minor hiccups:
- Forgot to exclude query movie initially
- Brief stumble on heap internals (recovered)

**Verdict:** Hire (H) / Strong Hire (SH)

---

## 🔹 Round 4 — Onsite Coding (DP / Combinatorics)

### Problem:
Count subsets where:
sum(subset) > total_sum / 2

Example:
[1,3,4], total = 8 → threshold = 4  
Valid → [1,4], [3,4], [1,3,4] → answer = 3

### Approach:
- Started with recursion (pick / not pick)
- ❌ Bug in base case → overcounting
- Switched to DP

💡 Key idea:
Once sum > threshold → all remaining subsets are valid

⚠️ Still had a counting mistake, but discussion was decent

**Verdict:** Leaning Hire (LH)

---

## 📊 Final Self-Evaluation

| Round | Rating |
|------|--------|
| ML Design | H / SH |
| Googliness | LH |
| Coding 1 | H / SH |
| Coding 2 | LH |

---

## 🧠 Honest Take

Strengths:
- ML depth
- Problem solving
- Abilit

reported.text: Count subsets whose sum is greater than half the total sum (e.g. [1,3,4] gives 3).

reported.text: Given a range [L, R], count the numbers whose binary representation contains "101" as a substring (digit DP).

title: Minimum Knight Moves on a Chessboard

reported.text: Find the minimum number of knight moves from (x1, y1) to (x2, y2) on a chessboard, or -1 if unreachable.
N tasks with dependencies [x, y] (x before y) form a DAG. Each task takes one day and independent tasks can run in parallel. Return the minimum number of days to finish everything.
Given 2N integers, pair them all up; each pair scores the GCD of its two numbers. Return the maximum total score (bitmask DP).

title: Balloon Burst Game on a Grid

reported.text: A binary grid holds balloons (1s). Hitting a balloon bursts its whole 4-connected group. Two players alternate optimally, first player starts; return the maximum number of balloons the first player bursts.
